figures.caption: Figure 5: Terminal-Bench-Dev results at the same prefix model. (A, B) TB-dev mean score across three attempts, plotted against (A) teacher-inference cost (in teacher model tokens) and (B) training cost (in teacher model tokens). OP-Short points from bottom to top corresponds to: 329 BC traces + 329 OP traces, K = 3 (329 questions); 329 BC traces + 329 OP traces, K = ∞ (329 questions); 720 BC traces + 720 OP traces, K = 3 (720 questions). Diamond markers indicate the per-run mean score for each SFT checkpoint (three independent TB-dev evals).

Figure 6: HotpotQA checkpoint selection. Note that the dev set are composed of 3000 medium-level questions, which are the same difficulty level as the questions the checkpoints were trained on, but easier than the final 7400+ difficult-level questions that we report the selected checkpoints’ final performance. The distributional difference is intentional to avoid selection bias, and it also explains why the dev set performance range (45–55%) looks a lot higher than the main text’s reported test performance, which is in the 35–40% range.

Figure 2: HotpotQA SFT test accuracies for the recipe instances in Table 1. All variants use the same 1000 medium-level training questions Qtrain; PURE-BC scales by sampling more i.i.d. teacher traces per question (n↑). Checkpoints are selected on a held-out dev set and then evaluated on the HotpotQA official test set (7.4k hard-level questions). Left: pass@1 versus teacher-inference cost Ci, measured in Qwen3 teacher output tokens generated during data construction. Right: the same pass@1 values versus retained training cost Ctr, measured in teacher tokens trained on per epoch. Error bars are one standard error estimated from 8 i.i.d. pass@1 evaluations on the full test set.

Table 5: Comparison of TB-dev evaluation scores for baseline models and Qwen3-8B under different SFT and RL settings. (numbers with * are from Openthoughts, others are from our implementation. Score is averaged across three attempts)

Figure 3: ALFWorld test accuracy on valid_seen pass@1. Left: The left panel counts total teacher labeling cost, including discarded. Right: the right panel counts teacher tokens retained for SFT. Note: for the case of 64 tasks 64, the traces are all filtered out under OP-CRITICAL, and thus there is no corresponding point.

Figure 9: Example trajectory from an InferredBugs command-line task. Purple denotes the full user prompt and task description, blue denotes terminal/environment observations, orange denotes student model actions up to Step 3, and green denotes teacher model actions from Step 4 onward.

Figure 8: Linearized schematic of the Figure 7 rollout trajectory as a sequential decision process. The agent’s next assistant turn generation, at, is sampled token by token, autoregressively from the conditional policy distribution πθ(·|ht−1).

Figure 7: A real ReAct-style rollout instantiating the sequential decision process in actual model output and token IDs. For each span, the top row shows abbreviated text and the bottom row shows corresponding token IDs (under a Qwen 2.5 tokenizer). The agent emits a reasoning trace and tool call (together as a1), receives a search result (o1), then boxes a final answer in a2. XML tags such as <tool_call>/</tool_call> delimit span boundaries in the raw sequence.
